title: One method in place of a validation framework

blocks.text: The page's first pitfall is an email check built as a rule framework:

The KISS fix is one method. Write `isValidEmail(String email)` in `Emails`. It looks only at the **first** `@` of the address, as the page's fix does with `indexOf('@')`, and returns `true` exactly when that `@` has at least one character before it and at least one after it. What those characters are does not matter: spaces or another `@` are allowed.

items: `isValidEmail("a@b@c")`, `isValidEmail("a@@")` and `isValidEmail("a b@c d")` are `true`: the first `@` has a character on each side;
`isValidEmail("@a@")` is `false`: nothing comes before its first `@`;

cases.says: "user@example.com" and "a@b@c" are valid and "userexample.com" is not.
null and "" are invalid, and checking them does not throw.
"@example.com" and "@a@" are invalid: something must come before the first @.
"user@" is invalid: something must come after the @.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A simple method replaces an over-engineered rule framework when one straightforward check is all the problem needs.
